title: Critical-path trace correlation and PD handover framework
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: create a resilient framework that (1) correlates distributed traces to active PagerDuty incidents, (2) produces a minimal, attack-surface-reduced evidence bundle attached to PD and Slack, and (3) surfaces candidate remediation steps and runbook snippets directly in the incident view. This ticket scopes the core infra, export format, and Slack/PD integration points for an MVP that reduces time-to-detection->acknowledge by providing actionable trace context.
motivation: Current incidents lack deterministic linkage to recent traces; oncall must hunt across traces, dashboards, and logs. That manual triage increases MTTI/MTTR and causes noisy escalations. A structured handover will make pages resolvable faster and reduce paging noise for low-information incidents.
acceptance_criteria: When a PagerDuty incident is created for a service with tracing enabled, the system attaches a compact evidence bundle to the incident within 45s containing: top 3 correlated traces, a condensed timeline, and key span attributes (service, span name, span id, error tags)
Slack incident channel receives a message with 'Investigate' quick-actions: open trace, jump to logs, add runbook tag, add suppression window
Evidence bundle size is capped (configurable, default 256KB) and redacts PII fields according to the observability-redaction policy
Oncall can trigger an auto-postmortem seed from the PD incident which creates a draft with top-3 hypothesis lines populated from trace annotations and previous incident history
No regression in PD integration latency (median < 200ms for metadata-only attachments) and platform cost increase under 5% for traced services at default sampling rates
implementation_notes: Create a lightweight evidence protobuf (evidence_v1) that flattens trace -> span summary + tag whitelist; include version header for backward compatibility
Leverage trace indexing service to compute 'critical path' by weighted error score and latency contribution; run scorer as async job triggered by the incident event
New endpoint /ops/handover that accepts incident_id, service_id, and a time window. It returns the evidence bundle and pre-signed URLs to full traces stored in internal trace storage
Attach evidence to PD via existing PD attachments API; for Slack use the ops-bot with ephemeral message + channel thread attachment for larger bundles
Implement redaction pipeline stage using the observability-redactor library; allow opt-out per-customer via privacy flag
Add feature flag (ff_critical_path_handover) to gate rollout and to allow gradual enable on staging -> canary -> prod
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: use a compact evidence format rather than full trace export to avoid PD attachment size limits and reduce leak surface
Tradeoff: summary computation is approximate (top-k heuristics) to meet latency SLO; this may miss low-frequency causal spans but reduces noise and cost
Decision: do not embed raw logs in the bundle; include traced log pointers (pre-signed URLs) to keep attachment small and meet compliance
Tradeoff: pre-signed URLs add TTL management complexity; we will reuse existing short-lived URL infra (30m default)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable ff_critical_path_handover for internal services and validate evidence structure with SRE
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% of customer traffic on hosted API with PD attachment throttling enabled
Phase 3 (prod): open to all customers with opt-out toggle and updated docs; monitor cost and PD error rates for 1 week
Post-release: run a 2-week oncall feedback loop to refine quick actions and hypothesis generation
monitoring_and_slo: Handover generation latency: p50 < 1s, p95 < 10s for metadata-only bundles
Error budget: track increased error surface from handover pipeline in observability-dashboards (handovers.errors)
privacy_and_compliance: By default redaction policy strips headers and tags matching regexes in observability/redact-rules (PII, auth tokens)
Opt-out customers: evidence pipeline will not include trace context beyond span ids and service metadata
Audit logs: every handover event writes an audit record with actor, incident_id, and evidence_version
blocking_issues: Need SRE signoff on evidence_v1 schema (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/2567)
Rate-limit policy for PD attachments needs final approval from platform-security (ticket SEC-1128)
Trace storage pre-signed URL bottleneck under heavy incident load — capacity planning requested (ENG-87090)
